[[File:Oil_tanker_Abqaiq_in_2003.jpg|thumb|right|A commercial oil tanker receives oil at a terminal off Iraq.]]
Total revenue of oil and gas companies is listed in billions of U.S. dollars. Total revenue is usually self-reported by companies, and often reported by neutral, unbiased, reliable publications. Reported data may be subsequently revised or restated due to a wide range of issues such as exchange rates, contract settlements, or mid-year discontinuation of products or services. Fiscal years are for January 1 to December 31, except where noted. Empty cells indicate that no data for that year has been reported yet.

This list is partially sourced from the [[S&P Global]] Commodity Insights Top 250 Global Energy Company Rankings for 2022. The S&P Global list is restricted to publicly traded companies, and only integrated oil and gas, oil and gas exploration and production, oil and gas refining and marketing, and oil and gas storage and transportation companies were included on the list below.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Commodity Insights Top 250 Global Energy Company Rankings|website=S&P Global|date=2022|access-date=April 21, 2022|url=https://www.spglobal.com/commodityinsights/top250/rankings}}</ref> For state-owned oil corporations, the list below is also partially sourced from data provided by [[Statista]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Revenues of largest state-owned oil companies worldwide in 2019 (in billion U.S. dollars)|website=Statista.com|date=2022|access-date=April 21, 2022|url=https://www.statista.com/statistics/793389/largest-state-owned-oil-companies/}}</ref> and the [[Sovereign Wealth Fund Institute]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Top 16 Largest National Oil Company Rankings by Total Assets|website=Sovereign Wealth Fund Institute|date=2022|access-date=April 21, 2022|url=https://www.swfinstitute.org/fund-rankings/national-oil-company}}</ref>

This list provides data for parent companies, not each subsidiary.
